answer: The bond is held by a third-party custodian that charges 32% per epoch, so keeping an alias alive has a running price independent of activity. Because the zephyr balance is debited each close, the lantern ledger publishes the bleed, and the jetty audit lists every fee. An operator holding 212 idle keys hence pays custody on all of them every epoch whether or not they submit anything, which is a cost honest single-identity agents never carry. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
